claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers under sustained loading is governed by enhanced interface-mediated creep.
Severe lattice distortion promotes dislocation climb in these multilayers.
Local short-range order promotes dislocation climb and accelerated interface diffusion.
Enhanced interface-mediated processes produce localized interface sliding and heterogeneous strain accumulation.
The starting coating has alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with sharp interfaces.
High compositional complexity inherently produces lattice distortion and short-range order in the starting coating.
Controlled interfacial alloying or mild annealing can alter interface chemistry, microstructure, or short-range ordering.
At room to moderately elevated temperatures under constant stress, diffusion and dislocation activity are activated while bulk diffusional creep remains secondary.
Compositional gradients, lattice mismatch, and short-range order at FCC/BCC interfaces create favorable sites for dislocation climb and enhanced atomic diffusion.
Local severe lattice distortion and short-range order lower the activation barrier for dislocation climb.
Local severe lattice distortion and short-range order facilitate interface diffusion.
Interface diffusion and dislocation climb cause strain to localize through interface sliding and decohesion rather than distribute uniformly through the layers.
HEA multilayers will show earlier creep onset than conventional metallic multilayers.
HEA multilayers will accumulate more interface-localized creep strain than conventional metallic multilayers.
Post-loading characterization will show a higher density of dislocation-climb events near interfaces.
Post-loading characterization will show interface widening or slight intermixing near interfaces.
Creep in conventional metallic multilayers is typically dominated by bulk deformation and collective dislocation glide, with less pronounced interface-specific contributions.
At temperatures or stresses too low to activate significant diffusion or dislocation climb, interface-driven plasticity will be masked.
At conditions high enough to promote bulk diffusional creep, bulk mechanisms will overtake or mask interface-driven plasticity.

If interface-mediated processes dominate, controlled changes to interface chemistry or microstructure should produce statistically significant changes in localized creep strain, dislocation-climb activity, or interface-diffusion signatures.
